ClassificationReview.description:
One classification a human is asked to check (T48, packet 028). The machine's answer is carried
WITH the excerpt it was derived from - a reviewer must never be asked to agree or disagree without
seeing the text the decision was made on (D6). ``conf`` is a rule-strength prior, not a probability
(see ajp.extract.evidence), and ``model`` names the version that produced it.
ClassificationReview.title: ClassificationReview

ClassificationReviewResponse.description:
The worklist plus the counts to judge it by. ``threshold`` and ``model`` are returned with the data
itself so a reader never has to guess what a 0.6 means or which model produced it.
ClassificationReviewResponse.title: ClassificationReviewResponse

OrgBoardBlocked.description:
One blocked board URL of one organisation, with the reason it was refused - so "degraded" is
always attributable to a specific URL rather than a bare status string.
OrgBoardBlocked.title: OrgBoardBlocked

OrgBoardHealthResponse.description:
Per-organisation health of the rs_org_boards fan-out, read from the per-org reports
run_ledger.http_counters already persists (see registry.fetch_org_board_health). The rollups let a
caller see the shape at a glance; `orgs` carries the attribution, degraded first.
OrgBoardHealthResponse.title: OrgBoardHealthResponse

ReviewDecisionIn.description:
A human's answer to one queued classification. 'corrected' REQUIRES human_kind - the DB enforces
the same rule, but failing at the schema layer returns a 422 that says so before the DB is touched.
ReviewDecisionIn.title: ReviewDecisionIn

ReviewDecisionOut.description:
What recording a human decision returns. ``applied`` is always False by contract: the correction is
RECORDED, never auto-written back to `listing` (the standing 'a human decision is recorded, never
auto-applied' ruling) - the field exists so the response says so explicitly instead of leaving a
reader to wonder whether their correction took effect silently.
ReviewDecisionOut.title: ReviewDecisionOut

info.description: Read-only listing API (M3, packet 007). Every uncertain field carries {v, conf, raw}; salary EUR/year figures always carry their fx basis; see /v1/meta.degraded_features for known gaps (never silently omitted).

get.description:
Per-organisation health of the rs_org_boards fan-out source, attributed by org slug.

Answers PM's own F4 finding (debug_sweep_2026-10-10.md): "rs_org_boards partially degraded - 3
sub-URLs tripped R1" was reported honestly but unactionably, because /v1/sources aggregates
crawl_state by source_id and returns reason strings with no attribution. This endpoint reads the
per-org reports run_ledger.http_counters already persists, so a degraded org is always paired with
the exact board URL and the reason it was refused.

Read-only, and it invents nothing: with no fan-out run recorded yet it returns zeroed rollups
rather than an error, so a fresh install is a valid empty answer rather than a 500.
